questions.text: Walk me through how you designed a CI/CD pipeline for a service you own. What stages did it have, and how did you keep deployments safe?

follow_up_suggestions.text: Which tools did you use for each stage, and why did you choose them?
How did you handle a failed deployment or a rollback?

scoring_rubric.2: Lists tools without explaining the flow or safety checks
scoring_rubric.3: Describes build, test and deploy stages with some safety measures
scoring_rubric.4: Covers staged rollout, automated tests and rollback clearly
scoring_rubric.5: Explains trade-offs, progressive delivery and how the design evolved

questions.text: Tell me about a time a Kubernetes workload failed in production. How did you find the cause and fix it?

follow_up_suggestions.text: What did the logs, metrics or events show you at each step?
How did you prevent the same failure from happening again?

scoring_rubric.1: Cannot describe a failure or its cause
scoring_rubric.2: Describes the failure but not the investigation
scoring_rubric.3: Explains a sensible investigation using logs or events and a fix
scoring_rubric.4: Shows systematic diagnosis and a preventive change
scoring_rubric.5: Explains root cause analysis, prevention and shared learning with the team

questions.text: How do you manage infrastructure changes safely when several teams depend on the same cloud resources?

follow_up_suggestions.text: What does your review or approval process look like in practice?
How do you know a change will not break another team?

scoring_rubric.2: Mentions reviews but no concrete safeguards
scoring_rubric.3: Uses infrastructure as code, plans and reviews
scoring_rubric.4: Adds state locking, staged environments and clear ownership
scoring_rubric.5: Explains policy guardrails, blast-radius limits and cross-team communication

questions.text: Describe how you set up monitoring and alerting for a service. How did you decide what should page someone?

follow_up_suggestions.text: Which metrics did you watch, and what thresholds did you choose?
How did you deal with alerts that fired too often?

scoring_rubric.2: Lists metrics without criteria for alerting
scoring_rubric.3: Uses symptom-based alerts with some tuning
scoring_rubric.4: Ties alerts to user impact and reduces noise deliberately
scoring_rubric.5: Explains SLOs, error budgets and a clear paging policy

questions.text: What would you check first if a deployment succeeded but users reported slow responses an hour later?

follow_up_suggestions.text: What would you look at in the first five minutes, and why?
How would you tell the affected teams what is happening?

scoring_rubric.3: Checks recent changes, dashboards and logs in a sensible order
scoring_rubric.4: Narrows the scope methodically and communicates status clearly
scoring_rubric.5: Also explains rollback decisions, customer impact and a follow-up review
